target.title: fix(telegram): attribute the bot's own chat-window messages as self
target.body:
Fixes #102267

## Problem

In the Telegram "Conversation context" chat window, the bot's own previously sent messages render with an anonymized sender label (for example "Agent3"), indistinguishable from any other participant. The agent reads its own past replies back as a stranger's messages, which corrupts multi-party reasoning and recap grounding.

## Fix

Three narrow changes:

- `extensions/telegram`: when building prompt-context messages from the cached conversation window, compare each cached message's `from.id` against the bot's own id (`ctx.me.id`) and stamp `is_self: true` on matches. Read-time comparison only; no stored fields are mutated.
- Self-message sender naming falls back through: configured account `name`, then the bot's own Telegram identity (`ctx.me.first_name`, then `ctx.me.username`), then the existing cached sender label. Real deployments commonly have no configured account name, so the identity fallback is what makes the fix effective out of the box.
- `src/auto-reply`: the chat-window renderer appends a self marker to self-marked messages, rendering them as `Name (you)`.

## Live verification (real Telegram)

Verified on a live Telegram DM exchange on 2026-07-09 against a deployed build of this change: the bot's own prior reply rendered in the "Conversation context" recap with the `(you)` marker, confirming the id-match fires on real traffic (request payloads inspected via tracing, not model self-report). That live run is also what motivated the identity fallback: with no configured account name, the sender previously fell back to the anonymized cached label.

## Notes

- Known edge, intentionally out of scope: replies recorded via the streamed path carry a sentinel message id, so they are not self-marked by this change; that gap exists today and will be reported separately.
- Tests: telegram-side coverage (self message carries `is_self` and the resolved name; configured-name precedence; identity fallback) and renderer coverage (`Name (you)` for self-marked messages, other senders unmarked). Two pre-existing fixtures' expected sender updates from a stale cached label to the correctly resolved bot username, which is the intended effect of the resolution chain.
